entries.notes: The applied text at l.237 is C-50's corrected text verbatim. The label at l.228 and the arrow notation at l.865 are named in `corrected`. (1) The definition. Lean's EGF.IsKernelErgodic pi mu says: for every measurable A, if pi x A = 1_A(x) for mu-almost every x, then mu A = 0 or mu A^c = 0. It holds for any kernel and asks no invariance of mu. The TeX gives the same clause for a Markov kernel, which is narrower, so Lean >= paper. 'This depends on mu only through its null sets' is EGF.isKernelErgodic_congr: if mu << nu and nu << mu, the two ergodicities are equivalent. (2) Kernel => group, for any weights. EGF.IsEGFPolicy.forall_of_isKernelErgodic covers any mu and any weights. It needs only IsEGFPolicy: Phi_i measurable, and alpha measurable, >= 0 and summing to 1, which is Definition 3.1's policy after C-27. Its conclusion is that every A with Phi_i^{-1}(A) =ae A for all i is null or conull. That is Definition 3.1's 'That is' clause verbatim (lambda(Phi_i^{-1}(A) symdiff A) = 0 iff Phi_i^{-1}(A) =ae A). EGF.isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_of_forall then lifts the generator form to IsGroupErgodic lambda (egfGroup Phi), with no hypothesis. So this direction needs no nonsingularity, which answers the dispatch's question. The listed anchor isEGFErgodic_of_isKernelErgodic carries hns (lambda.map Phi_i << lambda and lambda.map Phi_i^{-1} << lambda) only because it concludes the bundled IsEGFErgodic, whose `nonsingular` field belongs to the structure. Its proof uses only the .2 direction of isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_iff, which is isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_of_forall. In any case Definition 3.1's diffeomorphisms of a Riemannian manifold with its volume are nonsingular both ways, since the inverse is a diffeomorphism. That is formalized for Haar measure (EGF.nonsingular_of_diffeomorph), not for a general Riemannian volume (DefEGF SCOPE). (3) The converse, 'if every alpha^i > 0'. EGF.IsEGFPolicy.isKernelErgodic (UniversalityErgodic.lean:808) goes from the generator form with hpos (for all i and s, 0 < alpha i s), which is 'every alpha^i > 0' read pointwise. From the group form, the route is IsEGFErgodic.isKernelErgodic through isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_iff. That needs two-way nonsingularity, and EGF.FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall shows the need. Definition 3.1's setting supplies it, and its 'That is' states the generator form outright. The conclusions are the same, and so are the hypotheses: the TeX speaks of 'the policy of (equ:forward_policy)' with Definition 3.1's moves and weights. added_hypotheses lists the positive weights for the converse, and the TeX has them. Nothing else was added. (4) The refuted reading. The circle with Phi_1 the rotation by sqrt 2, Phi_2 = id and alpha = (0, 1) gives the identity kernel. Under the defined notion the identity kernel is not ergodic for lambda: every set is invariant. So Theorem 3.4 (l.304, 'ergodic for a finite invariant measure equivalent to lambda') no longer covers it, while the group stays ergodic, which is the 'any weights' direction. (5) Uses. Theorem 3.4 (l.304) and B.1 (l.855) read as IsKernelErgodic pi lambda-hat, the form of universal_iff_ergodic. B.1's Necessity (l.865) is the defined clause at mu = lambda-hat, and 0 < lambda(A) < lambda(S) is its negation, since lambda-hat ~ lambda. B.2's 'the policy alpha^i = 1/p is then ergodic for lambda' (l.888) is now justified by the converse. The Necessity line is otherwise byte-identical to C-39's text. ref{def:egf} renders as 3.1. Cosmetic: pi(x -> A) is first used in the main text here. Section 2 defines P(pi(x) in A) and mu (x) pi(A -> B) (l.162), and Appendix A writes pi*(s -> X). The notation reads, and the entry chose it to match Appendix A. See findings 1 and 2 for two uses this paragraph affects.

The applied texts at l.142 and l.222 are C-51's corrected texts verbatim. Checked against the cited source, brunswic2024theory section 3.5 (papers/nonacyclic/legacy/orig, pdftotext): 'A natural generalization of a cycle in the measurable setting is that of 0-flow, eg a flow of target R = 0. One notices that a 0-flow can be seen as a random transformation N of S* preserving some measure F_out.' Its Example 1 makes the irrational rotation with Lebesgue measure a 0-flow, and its Definition 9 speaks of a 'nontrivial 0-subflow'. A 0-flow is therefore a flow with zero source and sink, that is, a measure preserved by the kernel: xi pi* = xi. 'Non-zero' matches 'nontrivial' and the sentence's 'if such a xi exists' (xi = 0 always exists). The printed 'ergodic measures' named only the extreme 0-flows. Under C-50's definition, which asks no invariance, it would make lambda a '0-flow' of every EGF ergodic for lambda. The corrected wording removes both problems. It also makes l.508 ('0-flows directions', a cone of directions in which R's derivative is positive) consistent, which a set of ergodic measures is not. lean-egf does not formalize 0-flows. The entry is kind typo with no anchor, which the register's rules allow, and it is a convention fixed by the cited source, not a reading. walters2000introduction leaves l.222 and stays at l.145; main.bbl is unchanged (build). No hypotheses and no refutation. One precision point in the gloss is finding 3.

The applied text at l.801-803 is C-52's corrected text verbatim once the pre-existing C-48 marker line (l.802) is skipped. C-7's text (nonsingular, (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda) and C-48's 'differentiable' are kept, and so are the C-48 and C-7 markers. The anchor EGF.backward_policy assumes: any measurable space and measure; Phi : Fin p -> S equiv_m S; J measurable with lambda.map Phi_i = J_i lambda; IsEGFPolicy F.policy Phi alpha; F.outflow = f_out lambda with f_out measurable. Its corollary backward_policy_rnDeriv, the form of record with C-8's lambda-Jacobian (l.812), turns hJ into a sigma-finite lambda and the one-way hac: lambda.map Phi_i << lambda. Hypothesis by hypothesis: a differentiable manifold is weakened to a measurable space. The background lambda is finite by the standing assumption of l.165, hence sigma-finite. '(Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda' is hac, one way only, as the Lean needs. Diffeomorphisms are weakened to measurable equivalences. F_out = f_out lambda is hout. 'alpha is a measurable policy with sum_i alpha^i = 1' together with pi*(s -> .) = sum alpha^i delta_{Phi_i(s)} is IsEGFPolicy (alpha >= 0 through 'policy', alpha : S -> [0,1]^p of Definition 3.1, imported by 'As in Section 3'). 'Without the ergodicity clause ..., which this appendix does not use' matches backward_policy's docstring: 'No ergodicity is assumed (def:egf's clause is not used)'. Two-way nonsingularity enters only Definition 3.1's 'That is', which the appendix drops, so one way suffices. Lean >= paper. 'Consider a Generative Flow' replaces 'we define an EGF as', so v2 has one definition of EGF. added_hypotheses = [] is right: measurability and sum = 1 are C-27's declared added hypotheses, restated here to import them, not new. Not false, no refutation. The C-48 marker sits between the two edited lines, which is pre-existing and harmless.

The applied texts at l.762 and l.763 are C-56's corrected texts verbatim. (1) l.762, 'under which, for lambda invariant, the outflow is a convergent series (the remark after its proof)', repeats l.857 (C-29) and points to the remark at l.871 (C-21). That remark rests on EGF.tsum_mixingCoeff_self_ne_top_iff (with lambda-hat = lambda, summable iff some gamma_N < 1) and EGF.tvMass_construction (the lifted partial sums), both C-56 anchors. The remark says 'with lambda-hat = lambda' where the sentence says 'lambda invariant'. They agree through the chain CHECK-2 of T-egf-correct-ergodicity recorded at l.701: isKernelErgodic_of_isSummablyL2Mixing, Markov.ae_eq_const_of_densityAction_eq, trivial_of_lamHat_univ_eq_top. This is the wording v2 already uses at l.857, not an overclaim. (2) The move count at l.763. 'Theorems 3.5 and 3.6 ask only that the group generated by the moves be ergodic, respectively dense' is true of what the applied theorems ask of the moves (l.321: the group 'acts ergodically'; l.338: 'generate a dense subgroup'). They also ask C-31's rich model (finding 4, wording). 'Two transformations are sufficient', case by case: on T^2, EGF.universality_tori_of_matS_matT at p = 2 (A = ![S, T]). On T^d, d >= 2, EGF.universality_tori_sl with two generators of SL_d(Z) (conder2025generating, cited at l.325, not formalized), or more simply one move without periodic integer vector plus any other (EGF.universality_tori_of_mem_noPeriodic). On T^1, EGF.universality_tori_one: one translation of infinite order, whatever the other moves. On spheres, EGF.universality_sphere (density, any p) with two generators of a dense subgroup of SO(d+1). Lean instantiates n = 2 (so2Witness) and n = 3 (so3Witness: two rotations, listed with their inverses, generating the same subgroup), and none for n >= 4 (SphereDense SCOPE). So on S^d, d >= 3, the count rests on breuillard2003dense, as v2 l.342 already does. 'The inverses ... are not needed' holds because the theorems ask for the generated group, which contains the inverses. (3) The last clause, which the master kept: 'on T^d, d >= 2, a single affine move whose linear part has no periodic integer vector is already sufficient'. It is anchored as worded by EGF.universality_tori_single_move (ToriMinimal.lean:1018). That theorem covers any d and any M with IsUnit det M (GL_d(Z), which contains the SL_d(Z) of Aff(T^d)). Its NoPeriodicVector M is: for all k != 0 and n >= 1, M^n k != k. It holds for any translation and a rich model with p = 1, and concludes IsUniversalFamilyEps volume F. 'd >= 2' is where such an M exists: EGF.exists_universality_tori_single_move gives det M = 1 for d >= 2, while at d = 1, SL_1(Z) = {1}. The clause is the p = 1 case of the applied Theorem 3.5's own condition at l.321 ('contains an affine map whose linear part has no periodic integer vector'). It is also C-29's adopted finding, so it is within DEC-144's 'corrected accordingly' and DEC-141's strongest true form. The rich model is implicit, as for 'two'. The direct anchor universality_tori_single_move is missing from C-56's anchor list (finding 6a). No hypothesis added. Not false, no refutation.

findings.what: Three paraphrases leave out the invariant measure that the defined notion no longer carries. l.285 says 'The next theorem states that if the family contains an ergodic policy pi*, then the family is universal.' l.297 says 'Ergodicity alone ensures the convergence of phi pi^n only in the much weaker Cesaro sense, and this is enough for universality (Theorem 3.4, Appendix B.1).' l.857 says 'universality itself needs only ergodicity.' All three are C-29's applied texts. Before this batch the ergodicity of a kernel was undefined, and these sentences read in Walters' convention, where invariance is presupposed. C-50 now defines 'ergodic for mu' with no invariance, rightly, since EGF.IsKernelErgodic asks none. In that defined sense, ergodic for lambda does not give universality. Take Bool with uniform lambda and pi constant delta_true (EGF.Sink.pol, MixingCriteria.lean:1036). Only the empty set and S are invariant, so pi is ergodic for lambda. From F_init = delta_true to F_term = delta_false, every outflow a delta_true + b delta_false leaves the defect (1+b)(delta_true - delta_false), so delta F_init(S) + delta F_term(S) = 2(1+b) >= 2. This example is by hand, not formalized. EGF.Sink.not_isSummablyL2Mixing shows that this pi has no invariant lambda-hat ~ lambda. The Cesaro convergence of l.297 is von Neumann's theorem on L^2(lambda-hat) and needs the invariant lambda-hat as well. This is minor and not an overclaim. Each sentence is an informal paraphrase next to the precise statement: Theorem 3.4 at l.304 and B.1 at l.855 both say 'ergodic for a finite invariant measure equivalent to lambda'. 'An ergodic policy' names no measure, so it is incomplete rather than contradictory. l.857 sits inside B.1, where lambda-hat is in scope.

findings.what: The gloss in C-51's l.222 text, '..., $\xi\ForwardPolicyStar=\xi$, that is generative flows with $\Finit=\Fterm=0$', is short of exact. In v2's vocabulary (l.165) a generative flow is any pair (pi*, F_out*). F_init and F_term are given separately, and flow matching is the constraint (2). So 'generative flows with F_init = F_term = 0' leaves out 'satisfying (2)'. Only then is xi = F_out* invariant: F_init + xi pi* = F_term + xi with F_init = F_term = 0. In the cited source a 'flow' includes the conservation. The first clause (xi pi* = xi) is exact, and the gloss follows it, so nothing is overclaimed. answers.c50_nonsingularity: The direction kernel => group does not need nonsingularity. EGF.IsEGFPolicy.forall_of_isKernelErgodic gives Definition 3.1's 'That is' clause (the generator form) for any weights and any mu, from IsEGFPolicy alone. EGF.isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_of_forall lifts that clause to the group's ergodicity with no hypothesis. The anchor EGF.isEGFErgodic_of_isKernelErgodic carries two-way nonsingularity only because it concludes the bundled IsEGFErgodic, which has a `nonsingular` field. Nonsingularity is needed both ways to go from the group form to the generator form (EGF.isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_iff, with EGF.FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall showing it is needed), which is the route of the converse through IsEGFErgodic.isKernelErgodic. Definition 3.1's diffeomorphisms of a Riemannian manifold with its volume supply it, since the inverses are diffeomorphisms. That is formalized for Haar measure (EGF.nonsingular_of_diffeomorph), not for a general volume. 'This depends on mu only through its null sets' is EGF.isKernelErgodic_congr.
answers.c51_source: Confirmed against brunswic2024theory, section 3.5: a 0-flow is 'a flow of target R = 0 ... a random transformation N of S* preserving some measure F_out'. Its Example 1, the irrational rotation with Lebesgue measure, is a 0-flow. The corrected wording, a non-zero invariant measure, is the source's notion. The printed 'ergodic measures' named only the extreme ones.
answers.c52_backward_policy: Faithful. EGF.backward_policy_rnDeriv needs a sigma-finite lambda (lambda finite by l.165), one-way lambda.map Phi_i << lambda (the appendix's '(Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda'), IsEGFPolicy (the measurable policy summing to 1, with alpha in [0,1]^p from Definition 3.1) and F_out = f_out lambda. It assumes no ergodicity, as the appendix now says.
answers.c56_last_clause: Anchored as worded, by EGF.universality_tori_single_move: every d, every move x -> Mx + b with M in GL_d(Z) without periodic integer vector, every b, and a rich model give an epsilon-universal family. Existence for d >= 2 is EGF.exists_universality_tori_single_move (det M = 1). At d = 1 no such M exists, hence 'd >= 2'. It is the p = 1 case of the applied Theorem 3.5's own clause (l.321), and C-29's adopted finding. The anchor list should name universality_tori_single_move (finding 6a).
answers.c57: Faithful to EGF.isSummablyL2Mixing_of_pow_contraction, modulo Gelfand's formula (spectral radius < 1 gives some N with ||T^N|| < 1), which is standard and not formalized, as at l.300. All three refutations are excluded.
answers.l145: Not real. 'Provable guarantee with an ergodicity assumption of the group generated by the EGFs transformations' is exact for Theorems 3.5-3.6.
